searchText: I didn’t code mIRC itself. I learned the native coding language to create scripts, software, bots, themes, etc.. - MIRC scripting language (mSL) is the name .. but it is very “universal” (not sure if that’s a good word) example from a search bot i@made on *:text:!search*:#sat: { msg # Searching for $+(", $+ $2- $+ ,"). var %find.found 0 🤷 I don't think "the community" understands the tradeoff being made. See Polygon/BSC as case studies of people being surprised by state bloat after they run with crazy high gas bandwidth for a while. Maybe in 6 months they will, based on these experiments 😅 But I tend to agree, and also think that some may get the tradeoff and be OK doing it for the short-term benefits because they won't be there to deal with the long term consequences, and that's very hard to tell Thank you, Micah! ❤️ I'm looking for transaction data that includes signatures values. Is there a way where I can easily obtain this, or should I just run a node and write custom code to dump the data? (Doesn't seem to be available on EtherScan or the BigQuery dataset.) <@!218397452309495809> something like this? ``` $ ethereal transaction info --transaction=0x26f9d6c16b1833c7491635a6911897798c0687e95ed8e334b699cc3a619a59e7 --json {"nonce":"0x337a","gasPrice":"0x5d21dba00","gas":"0xd6d8","to":"0x9aab071b4129b083b01cb5a0cb513ce7eca26fa5","value":"0x0","input":"0xa9059cbb000000000000000000000000388942a7f7cfab7ead1e72f6e787bf9e65630bba00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000209354483b5588000","v":"0x25","r":"0xe52c06683d3bdc6bb740f62d127d0f490c18ed36538eda2c61bd77121cfc60ce","s":"0x3a9051843c1d9103a6e1171887e8d968052fd18b699eef718e595acd82f9ee02","hash":"0x26f9d6c16b1833c7491635a6911897798c0687e95ed8e334b699cc3a619a59e7"} ``` Yes, that's perfect 👍 https://github.com/wealdtech/ethereal Nice, looks like I'll need to run a node anyway, but this makes it very easy to query! You can supply a connection, for example your own infura link. If you are going to pull down lots of data you'd be better off with your own node, but if it's only occasional requests infura should be fine. Hi all! new on here, sorry if my question has been talked about before (it most likely did) been asking around and someone pointed out this discord group for the answer. im running validators, and was wondering when withdrawal will be available if we will be able to withdraw only the rewards and keep the validator running or this hasn’t been determined yet? Thx withdrawals will likely be available at a fork soon after the merge and there are designs under consideration for withdrawing any ETH in excess of the 32 ETH base I think it is very likely such a proposal makes it in there. Otherwise, it incentivizes high churn on the validator set is mev-incentivized block orphaning a valid reason for an accelerated merge? <:peepothink2:754852084121206824> https://twitter.com/mevintern/status/1413133648036040704 in theory for eg. a big hack or liquidation bounty it could mean hours of chain being constantly orphaned as pools battle for supremacy most of the big pools don't run mev-geth plus 100 eth is less than 50 blocks of income. he was writing about over 100 eth, so it could as well be 50k eth (hack most likely) some orphaning is already happening. I know of cases of trades on taichi being frontrun in non-sparkpool blocks. which means someone started constructing them after seeing the original block, so it was intentional

sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I don't think "the community" understands the tradeoff being made.  See Polygon/BSC as case studies of people being surprised by state bloat after they run with crazy high gas bandwidth for a while.

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: Maybe in 6 months they will, based on these experiments 😅  But I tend to agree, and also think that some may get the tradeoff and be OK doing it for the short-term benefits because they won't be there to deal with the long term consequences, and that's very hard to tell
